A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CAAT-Net. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including material relocated between sections.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix D report original model-training results, zero-shot evaluations, synchronization and compression experiments, and training/inference timing measurements.

after.justification: Section 5 and Appendix E retain original experiments and add GPT-XL evaluations, numerical-precision and scaling ablations, TinyLlama synchronization sweeps, and NVIDIA timing measurements.

M1.justification: Private-channel correction changes from scaling weights at initialization in v1 Section 3.2 to multiplying activations by the corrective factor in v2 Section 4. V2 also introduces sequential logical-device inference with local summation when using fewer physical devices. The central partial-reduction and backward-synchronization procedures remain.

E1.justification: Both versions use RedPajama and the same seven evaluation benchmarks, alongside validation loss, training throughput and inference latency. Added experiments vary model architectures, synchronization, precision and hardware within these retained tasks; they introduce no new datasets or task requirements.

E2.justification: Fully synchronized models remain the accuracy and speed comparators, and Top-K and random masking remain the compression comparators. The added NVIDIA experiments use a different implementation framework but retain the full-all-reduce reference method.

E3.justification: Llama2-7B training increases from 90B to 160B tokens. V2 introduces a TinyLlama synchronization sweep, GPT3-XL training over 50B tokens, NVIDIA inference experiments using gpt-fast, and controlled precision/scaling experiments. These substantially expand experimental configurations and protocols.

E4.justification: V2 adds direct bfloat16-versus-fp32 accumulation experiments showing instability after approximately 15K steps (Appendix E.1), private-channel scaling ablations (E.3), and synchronization sensitivity across TinyLlama configurations. GPT-XL and NVIDIA experiments additionally test architecture and hardware robustness beyond v1's evidence.

E5.justification: Accuracy uncertainty margins appear in both versions. V2 additionally reports Welch's t-test, identifying the 7B BoolQ difference as marginally significant with p-value 0.046 and describing other accuracy differences as nonsignificant. Neither version specifies additional repeated runs or seeds.

E6.justification: Table 1 replaces the 7B results after longer training: baseline/CAAT-Net BoolQ changes from 62.75/62.29 to 64.89/62.51. TinyLlama scores and 130M curves are revised; GPT-XL, expanded synchronization and NVIDIA results are added. Training throughput values also change, including TP16 at p=0.25 from 110190 to 112456 tokens/s. These are revised or newly reported results, not established same-setting gains. Existing 34B/70B inference measurements are retained.

T1.justification: V2 generalizes the stated backward-pass derivation from RMSNorm to arbitrary normalization functions, including LayerNorm, and removes v1's Top-K MMSE-optimality assertion. The MLP/attention definitions, residual-gradient reasoning and Appendix C speedup derivation are otherwise retained, despite relocation and renumbering.

C1.justification: The central communication-reduction and acceleration claims remain. V2 qualifies the abstract's accuracy claim with 'across nearly all evaluated benchmarks' and describes accuracy as 'largely on par' in the contributions, while elevating possible validation-loss improvements into the abstract.

C2.justification: V2 adds the ensemble interpretation at zero synchronization, explains the computation-graph distinction, and discusses optional scaling and hardware-buffer alignment as accuracy/speed considerations. It removes v1's explicit caution about generalizing small-model trends and treating validation loss as a proxy. The training-speed projection limitation remains.

D1.justification: V2 adds a source-code link, NVIDIA device and NVLink specifications, the gpt-fast implementation reference, and GPT-XL configuration details. It also specifies training-speed micro-batches of 4 for TP4 and 8 for TP8/16; these disclosures alone do not establish changes to the corresponding earlier settings.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations for context parallelism, LayerNorm and RMSNorm. It expands discussion of the already-cited Ladder Residual method and explains how competing communication demands motivate complementarity with overlap methods. The overall research positioning remains.

P1.justification: V2 substantially reorganizes the exposition: attention equations move to Appendix A, channel scaling moves into implementation, large-scale and synchronization experiments are combined, and compression accounting moves to Appendix D. The abstract, architectural explanation, inference discussion and experimental narrative are also rewritten.

P2.justification: Figures 3 and 4 become expanded multipanel displays, the compression table becomes Figure 5, and new diagnostic Figures 6–7 and evaluation tables are introduced. Architecture diagrams and captions are revised. The earlier 34B/70B speedup plots disappear, while their numerical tables remain.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens empirical support for important implementation requirements through direct precision and scaling ablations, and tests robustness across synchronization levels, architectures and hardware. The code link and explicit BoolQ significance qualification improve reproducibility information and claim calibration. Training-speed evidence remains a 16-bit projection, and the retained 14% speedup statement conflicts with the approximately 16.4% implied by the revised Table 6. These reporting limitations temper, but do not outweigh, the substantial gains in supporting evidence.
